subject: aftf
title: (R)AFTF.------TH.CONT.
description: Diagram in CMOA(I)-9 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — Britain/Germany/Holland) accompanying Braxton's claim about the post-Webern movement and the late-fifties emergence of European improvisation: 'the creativity which I have been experiencing in the last ten years can clearly be looked at as a separate creative thrust that is distinctly European in its vibrational identity and directly coupled to the challenge of world music.' (R)AFTF (the reality of affinity transfer) is crossed with TH-CONT (thrust continuance): the question is what affinity-transfer produces in its actual instantiation when crossed with thrust-continuance — under conditions where Europe is forging a creative identity distinct from American improvised music. TH-CONT sits at the upper-center. TF-SH (transfer shift) anchors the upper-right output. T-C-IMP (time continuum implications) sits between subject and partner. CRTF-D (cross-transfer definitions) hangs on the lower-right via a *dashed* edge to T-C-IMP — conditional. POL-SIGN (political significance) anchors the bottom via another *dashed* edge to T-C-IMP. Structural argument: affinity-transfer-as-real crossed with thrust-continuance is mediated by time-continuum-implications as central hub. The unusually sparse diagram (only 5 nodes) is itself structurally significant: Braxton is making a focused argument about what European improvisation requires — affinity-transfer actually obtaining (the (r)), thrust-continuance as crossing-partner, temporal-continuity as hub, and transfer-shift as output. The two dashed edges (T-C-IMP→CRTF-D and T-C-IMP→POL-SIGN) are load-bearing diagnostic: cross-transfer-definitions and political-significance are only *conditional* outputs of this crossing — the European improvised music scene can achieve transfer-shift without necessarily achieving cross-transfer-definitions or political-significance, which is why the next pages will distinguish productive from unproductive European movements.
